evidence.api_compatibility: No public API is changed. The container image tag `candidate` is a new publication target; existing users of `latest`, `edge`, or `v<version>` tags are unaffected. The tools/version.py argparse change is an internal parsing refactor with no external contract.
evidence.documentation: docs/guide/install/docker.md was updated with a table documenting the three rolling tags (latest, candidate, edge) and the versioned variant tags. The new `candidate` tag documentation is clear and complete. No guide or example is needed for this CI-only change.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The PR introduces a new user-reachable artifact: the `candidate` Docker tag (ghcr.io/lemonade-sdk/lemonade-server:candidate) and the `candidate-v<version>` immutable tag. No evidence exists that a human pulled and exercised these tags before merge. The PR author self-identified as "no docker expert" and asked for the work to be checked. The to-do above is the concrete action to verify.
evidence.post_approval_commits: One commit was added after @superm1's first and only approval (submitted at 2026-09-14T19:51:50Z): the argparse refactor of tools/version.py (sha 2da5cc76, committed 2026-09-14T19:59:00Z). The commit message states it was "Review feedback" to replace argv scanning with argparse. This is a minor code-quality improvement that changes the internal parsing logic but does not alter the external behavior, API, or security posture of the workflow. It is within the spirit of the approved PR and does not warrant re-approval, though the reviewer was not notified of the addition via a new review request.
evidence.review: PR #3581 had one substantive human review from @superm1 (state: APPROVED, submitted 2026-09-14T19:51:50Z). @superm1 is the named maintainer with subject matter expertise in "Docker, containers" per docs/dev/contribute.md, so the review meets the expertise bar. The review body was empty; @jeremyfowers acknowledged in the PR description "I'm no docker expert so please check the work here," which invites scrutiny that was delivered as a terse approval. A Codex bot review flagged a real race condition on the rolling `candidate` tag: when two pushes to a release-v* branch run concurrently without a `concurrency` policy, an older build can finish last and overwrite the tag with stale code. That comment was never addressed or resolved. The Codex bot (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]) is automated, not a human reviewer.
evidence.security: The changes add a new CI publication path (release-v* branches push to ghcr.io) and a scheduled branch-creation workflow. The scheduled workflow uses a GitHub App push (not GITHUB_TOKEN) to trigger candidate builds, which is a deliberate security boundary. No credential handling, supply-chain, or obfuscation concerns. The Codex-identified race condition (stale tag overwrite) is a correctness concern, not a security issue.
evidence.tests: This is a CI/infrastructure change with no new user-facing code. There are no unit tests or integration tests; the CI validation workflows (llama.cpp, stable-diffusion.cpp, vLLM) all passed on the merge commit. No test weakening or deletion is present.

maintainer_todos.text: Pull ghcr.io/lemonade-sdk/lemonade-server:candidate on a machine and confirm the container starts and serves the same API version as the associated release-v branch.
